question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-150 (Collect Data from Common Resource Locations) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

answer.headline: Gathered 7 record(s) from 2 source(s); 6 cross-source correlation(s) on shared identifiers.
answer.narrative: CAPEC-150 (Collect Data from Common Resource Locations) maps to the ATT&CK techniques T1003, T1119, T1213, T1530, T1555, and T1602. Mitigations for these techniques include Encrypt Sensitive Information (M1041), which is associated with most of them, alongside others like Password Policies (M1027) and Privileged Account Management (M1026) for credential-related techniques. For repository-based techniques, mitigations such as Audit (M1047), Software Configuration (M1054), and User Account Management (M1018) are also listed.

records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An adversary exploits well-known locations for resources for the purposes of undermining the security of the target. In many, if not most systems, files and resources are organized in a default tree structure. This can be useful for adversaries because they often know where to look for resources or files that are necessary for attacks. Even when the precise location of a targeted resource may not be known, naming conventions may indicate a small area of the target machine's file tree where the resources are typically located.
